pairs.why: B's table is a slab top on a straight-sided square pedestal with plain cylindrical stools, like the real flat-faced stone block, while A's flared, waisted pedestal and spool-shaped stools are rounded and toy-like.
B's pack has tighter, more upright flat faces, a thin handle and thin straps, and a slimmer roll, whereas A is puffed into a fat pillowy blob with an oversized roll.
B's clock is a slightly shallower, thinner-rimmed disc with a flat face, closer to the real card than A's thick puffy tube rim, though B is tilted like a standing clock.
A's rock is a faceted irregular lump with a clear flame silhouette, closer to the real objects' crisp planes than B's smooth blobby potato with big round holes.
A's table has a thin flat top on a straight block pedestal on a slab base, matching the real card's boxy form, but B is nearly the same, so the gap is small.
A's pump is a tall tapered block with a flat panel and a thin hose, matching the real boxy body, while B adds extra parts like a louvered grille and a tall sign.
B's hat has a flatter, thinner brim and a straight cone with a crisp buckle, while A's soft drooping cone and thick floppy brim read as blobby.
B has the real card's slim, many-part build with thin rods, rails and a grille, while A is a chunky blocky toy with fattened parts and a squat wedge nose.
